components.gap: Durrett's justificatory claim at the opening of sec. 1.4 (PTE5 author version of 11 January 2019, p. 18) is not reported anywhere on the route: he develops the integral for a general sigma-finite measure rather than only for probability measures because integrals against infinite measures are sometimes needed and, he says, the general development is no harder. The route reports only the sigma-finite hypothesis itself and its removal (body lines 26-27; w02b-p15-001 lines 38-40; w02c-p15-005 lines 46-49), not the reason. Supply this claim with its p. 18 locator, for example beside body lines 26-27.
components.basis: Present: the definition at body lines 25-45 fixes a measure space with no finiteness or sigma-finiteness assumption, the disjoint-partition representation with finite nonnegative coefficients, the simple integral and the extended products (zero times infinity is zero, a positive finite number times infinity and infinity times infinity are infinity), with the zero-valued region of infinite measure as worked boundary; independence of representation is proved at annex lines 12-27. Source variant (Durrett PTE5 sec. 1.4, p. 18: signed simple functions on disjoint pieces of finite measure, sigma-finite measure) is identified at body lines 11-16, annex lines 244-250, and the sigma-finite standing hypothesis at w02b-p15-001 lines 38-40 and w02c-p15-005 lines 46-49.

(matching Durrett's a.e. definition, p. 18), measurability and no silent completeness. components.gap: Durrett's justificatory claim on p. 26 (PTE5 author version of 11 January 2019) for stating his bounded convergence theorem, Theorem 1.5.3, under convergence in measure is not reported on the route: having noted that on a space of finite measure this is a weaker assumption than a.e. convergence, he says the theorem is easier to prove in that greater generality. w02c-p15-005 lines 139-166 report only the first half of that sentence and the containment of the a.e. version. Supply the reason with its p. 26 locator, for example after body line 235.

components.gap: Durrett's framing of this theorem on p. 30 (PTE5 author version of 11 January 2019) is not reported: he introduces it as a further integration-to-the-limit result that his later developments need, and singles out g(x) = |x|^p with p > 1 and h(x) = x as perhaps its most important special case. Body lines 421-423 give that case only as an example, and no route text reports his evaluation of it or the role he assigns to the theorem. Supply the claim with its p. 30 locator.
